sutta: 7.10. On one occasion, the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket. Now, on that occasion, 14 oxen belonging to a certain brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan had gotten lost. Then the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan was searching for those oxen. Went to the woodland thicket where the Blessed One was staying. There he saw the Blessed One sitting with his legs folded crosswise, holding his body erect, having set up mindfulness in front of him. Having seen him, he approached the Blessed One and recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One. "Surely this ascetic does not have 14 oxen that have gotten lost, not seen now for the past 6 days. Hence, this ascetic is happy. Surely this ascetic does not have a field of blighted sesame plants, some with one leaf, some with two. Hence, this ascetic is happy. Surely this ascetic does not have rats inside an empty barn dancing around merrily. Hence, this ascetic is happy. Surely this ascetic does not have a blanket that for 7 months has been covered with swarms of vermin. Hence, this ascetic is happy. Surely this ascetic does not have seven daughters left for widows, some with one son, some with two. Hence, this ascetic is happy. Surely this ascetic does not have a tawny wife with pockmarked face who wakes him up with a kick. Hence, this ascetic is happy. Surely, this ascetic does not have creditors who call at dawn chiding him, "Pay up. Pay up." Hence, this ascetic is happy. So, when the Buddha heard him speak this so, the Buddha replied, "Surely, Brahmin, I do not have 14 oxen that have gotten lost, not seen now the past 6 days. Hence, Brahmin, I am happy. Surely, Brahmin, I do not have a field of lighted sesame plants, some with one leaf, some with two. Hence, oh Brahmin, I am happy. Surely, Brahmin, I do not have rats inside an empty barn dancing around merrily. Hence, oh Brahmin, I am happy. Surely, Brahmin, I do not have a blanket that for 7 months has been covered with swarms of vermin. Hence, oh Brahmin, I am happy. Surely, Brahmin, I do not have seven daughters left for widows, some with one son, some with two. Hence, oh Brahmin, I am happy. Surely, Brahmin, I do not have a thorny wife with pockmarked face who wakes me up with a kick. Hence, oh Brahmin, I am happy. Surely, Brahmin, I do not have creditors who call at dawn chiding me, "Pay up. Pay up." Hence, oh Brahmin, I am happy. And this was said, and the Brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan said to the Blessed One, "Magnificent, Master Gotama. Magnificent." And he took refuge in the Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha and asked to go forth, and later he also became an arahant. So, these verses here are quite amusing.
